PC , PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series S , Xbox Series X
M For Mature 17+ // Blood, Nudity, Sexual Themes, Strong Language, Violence
Enter the world of Thedas, a vibrant land of rugged wilderness, treacherous labyrinths, and glittering cities – steeped in conflict and secret magics. Now, a pair of corrupt ancient gods have broken free from centuries of darkness and are hellbent on destroying the world. Thedas needs someone they can count on. Rise as Rook, Dragon Age’s newest hero. Be who you want to be and play how you want to play as you fight to stop the gods from blighting the world. But you can’t do this alone – the odds are stacked against you. Lead a team of seven companions, each with their own rich story to discover and shape, and together you will become The Veilguard.
After 100 hours and 3 playthroughs of Dragon Age: The Veilguard, I feel justified in my ten-year wait and satisfied by the results.

I have played through this game cover to cover. If it had no attachment to the IP I would give it a 4 out of 10. Good Points: it is a pretty game. It does pay for human voice actors. The first biggest hurdle is in isn't an RPG and it certainly isn't a return to form for Bioware, who is famed for created some of the best RPGs of the 1990s-2000s. Veilguard is aimed at a preteen audience, (there are LGBTQ+ options for both your character) as well as outside characters. As the poor character writing and poor plot writing are the hallmarks of this game I wouldn't get your hopes up as a player. All but one party member is entirely flat (undeveloped character). This is the snark supportive main character (pick any of the three options it changes nothing), who everyone will agree with, believe, and in time worship because they are always right, good, moral, and incapable of making mistakes except to continue the plot (those are scripted and entirely unmissable). Let me explain the one star review. For a game that uses an IP, sets expectations, and sells their game under a specific genre (there is then expectation that you will actually deliver the product your promise). Veilguard isn't an RPG, it isn't set within the world it claims to be, and there are few to no choices of any consequence (one of the hallmarks for a REAL RPG). Gameplay is interesting for 30 minutes to an hour maximum, there are less than twenty enemies in the game and all enemies are reskins of these few opponents (with bosses occasionally adding something more). If you would like to enjoy the game play it on normal or lower, the only addition difficulty adds is increasing the health copious amounts. Also being a long term God of War fan the comparsion is insulting. This is not a good action RPG game, this is one that never evolves or changes from the moment you begin as Rook to the final battle nothing notable changes. Daniel Daniel Daniel #HM044997 Member since 2025-04-28 1 Reviews Following 0 Topics 0 Users Follow Followed 0 Followers View 3 /10 I would have to disagree with those that are lauding the game as revolutionary or even a "Dragon Age" game. To perspective, I played through the game 3 different times. Doing different playthroughs to see what more you can get out of the game. Without spoilers, in terms of backstory, I would advise picking the Shadow Dragons or the Wardens to get the most out of the game. Starting with the character creator, I would agree that the game is better than its processors. You can make some genuinely beautiful characters and I can only imagine what it would be like to play this game with the modding community. However, it does fall short with certain elements. Mostly figure. I noticed that if trying to make more vivacious figured characters, the game fell quite short, despite some NPC character models showing that the capacity was there. I would've liked further, particularly considering other games in the future, to allow for more customization. Again, NPCs seemed to have far more uniqueness than your character which, in this day in age of an RPG, is a bit saddening. Graphics actually are pretty good in general. Sometimes it is delightful just looking at the scenery. They did good even with the occasional blurs here and there. However, my gripe isn't about that, as it is still pretty decent. What got me to the point of ranking the game to this level are two factors. Lore, RPG elements, and dialogue. THIS.... is what had me the MOST disappointed. Because this isn't just a simple RPG game. If you are a true fan that read all the Codex files, enjoyed creating different aspects within the Dragon's Keep and seeing your game from different lights... I am hard-pressed to see how you would enjoy the game as the lore breaks what has been established. With the character limit, I can't go into detail as I'd like, but to put it lightly... This game only works as a Dragon Age game... if it's treated as an alternate universe. DA fans deserved better and more care for this title. 2025-04-28 19:12:33 Like Dislike Copy
